title: TEST — production character sheets, and what a museum reference buys at the character level
revision: v1 — 2026-08-22 · Philipp's proposal after seeing a production character-sheet example (turnaround + back view + detail callouts)
_why: Our 1a sheets are 3-view turnarounds (front / 3/4 / profile). Philipp's example adds a BACK view and isolated
DETAIL CALLOUTS of worn/held items (collar, clasp, clutch, boot) — the production-grade format, and what the
Higgsfield 'character-sheet' workflow calls 'turnaround' (4 views incl. back) + 'triple panel' (detail close-ups).
A. FORMAT: does the production format (back view + callouts) hold character + prop consistency better?
B. THE PRODUCT QUESTION: when the held/worn object IS a museum artefact, what does injecting the registry
reference buy us versus generating from the description alone? Side by side, same seed discipline,
measured against the artefact's invariants. This is 'is it really the asset' at the character level.
Higgsfield character-sheet workflow (loaded 2026-08-22): turnaround = 'front view, 3/4 view, side profile, and
back view'; triple panel = 'full body, chest-up portrait, and detail close-up of face and accessories';
'Consistency is the product'; negative tail 'no text, no watermark, no logos, no frame borders'; 'original
character only'; mature adult structure. DELIBERATE OVERRIDE: the workflow says 'no props' — for artefact
sheets the held object is the point, so props are allowed and the override is stated.
Faces are never named persons (the victor is a composite, already in the registry identities).

subtest_A_format.subject: the 1a Workman and Archaeologist (already approved 3-view sheets)
subtest_A_format.what: Regenerate each as a PRODUCTION sheet: four-view turnaround (facing camera / turned 45° / side / from behind) PLUS a callout strip of the held and worn items isolated and enlarged — workman: the pick, the headcloth knot, the sash, the shoe; archaeologist: the bowler, the jacket front with its lapel/collar, the measuring staff, the boot.
subtest_A_format.consistency_method: GenHQ method #1: @image = the approved 3-view sheet as the identity reference; text = the character description; layout described WITHOUT nameable words (no 'FRONT/BACK/PROFILE' — they become captions).
subtest_A_format.gate: NEVER lists as before; exploratory pass; the callout items must be the SAME objects as in the views (pick head shape, bowler brim, staff length). Resolves the archaeologist's lapel inconsistency by making the jacket a callout.
subtest_A_format.measures: prop consistency across 4 views + callouts (pass/fail per item); any text.

subtest_B_artefact.subject: The Crowning's VICTOR (registry identity 'victor') wearing the KOTINOS (SM_RV_16)
subtest_B_artefact.why_this_one: We have the registry invariants, the 3D model, an existing scene, and a known failure history — v1 of The Crowning invented fresh green wreaths in shots 2 and 4 when the reference did not travel. The artefact is distinctive (dried golden-brown, narrow lanceolate leaves, wire ties, cloth-bound join, OPEN ring). A generic 'olive wreath' is the exact cliché the reference must defeat.

arms.WITHOUT: Production sheet of the victor wearing 'an olive wreath' — the registry reference NOT injected; description of the wreath limited to what a model would assume. Callout of the wreath.
arms.WITH: Identical prompt + @image = the SM_RV_16 museum render injected as the wreath reference + the registry identity invariants (dried golden-brown, narrow pointed leaves densely packed, wire ties, pale cloth wrap at the join, open ring). Callout of the wreath.

subtest_B_artefact.discipline: Same character reference, same composition, same negative tail, same model; only the artefact reference + invariants differ. Best-of-N each, pick the best of each arm (not the worst of WITHOUT).

measures.per_invariant: dried golden-brown (not green) · narrow lanceolate leaves · dense packing · wire ties present · cloth-bound join · OPEN ring (not closed) — pass/fail each, both arms
measures.callout_vs_reference: the enlarged wreath callout beside the real SM_RV_16 render in the Review Room — the 'is it the same object' view
measures.consistency: is the wreath the same wreath in all four views + the callout

subtest_B_artefact.expected: WITHOUT reverts to the cliché (fresh green, closed, no ties); WITH holds the invariants. If WITH does NOT hold, that is the more important result — it means the reference alone is insufficient at the character level and we need the deterministic/3D route for worn artefacts too.
subtest_B_artefact.not_asserted: nothing about a real person; the victor is a composite. The kotinos is the Athens 2004 object, not ancient — stated in the ledger as always.

optional_subtest_C.subject: Tentoglou's shoes (SM_RV_18) on a long-jumper; or the torch (SM_RV_12) in the runner's hand
optional_subtest_C.why: A worn object with an INSCRIPTION (8.41 / TOKIO) tests whether the reference keeps text faithful at character scale — the hardest case. Run only if B is clean.
optional_subtest_C.note: the torch in hand is Trailer A's a4/a6 problem in miniature.

review: All outputs into the Review Room under a new TEST section: each sheet beside its references; for B, the WITH and WITHOUT callouts beside the real SM_RV_16 render. Philipp judges. Ledger per image.
owner: empirica-imagegen (generation + gates); storyboard (spec, review room, verdict)
cost_note: Image-only; no video. Nano Banana Pro via Higgsfield.

RESULTS_2026-08-22.B_product_question: WITH 5/6 invariants (hue agreement 0.978 on all 3 candidates) vs WITHOUT 1/6 (stable fresh-green closed cliche). The reference carries the OBJECT. Verified by storyboard by eye.
RESULTS_2026-08-22.A_format: workman PASS; archaeologist v1 FAILED callout consistency (jacket) -> costume ruling: 1870s high-buttoned lapelled sack coat -> v2 PASS (sha 3f4921419247).
RESULTS_2026-08-22.C_inscriptions: REFUTES sheet-first for TEXT. Object held in every view; inscriptions LEGIBLE AND WRONG: 8.41 -> 8.71 (fabricated claim about a living athlete in his own hand), TOKIO vs TOKITO on the two shoes in one panel, Greek name garbled. Callout rescues legibility, not accuracy - worse, because legible-and-wrong reads as authoritative.
RESULTS_2026-08-22.NEW_HAZARD: The Greek name appeared although the prompt withheld it: the REFERENCE supplied text the prompt did not ask for (inverse of the torch). asserts_text:[] governs the prompt only; nothing yet guards the reference side.
RESULTS_2026-08-22.STANDING_RULE_AS_CORRECTED: Sheet-first for form/material/structure (proven). For any inscribed surface: TURN AWAY or CROP it, even inside the callout; inscriptions ride the ledger. Pre-crop reference images so they carry no inscribed surface the shot does not assert. Certify text only by character-level diff; never certify an ambiguous glyph.
